title: Mars fault-reactivation parameters
description: Converted from Modeling_Parameters in data/source/Mars_Parameter_Spreadsheet.xlsx. Values are the spreadsheet Value column. min/max come from Uncertainty/Range, with the hand fixes listed in range_fix_log.

parameters.name: Young's Modulus (Intact Basalt)
parameters.note: Schultz (1993) lab value for intact unfractured basalt; up to 100 GPa used in elastic flexure models (Grott & Breuer 2008, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2007.08.015).

parameters.name: Young's Modulus (Fractured Rock Mass)
parameters.note: Schultz (1993) effective deformation modulus for jointed/heavily fractured upper basaltic crust.

parameters.name: Poisson's Ratio
parameters.method: Direct tensile testing in lab & lithosphere modeling
parameters.note: Standard value across Martian tectonic and flexural modeling (Schultz 1993; Watters 2003, doi:10.1029/2002JE001934).

parameters.name: Cohesion (Intact Basalt)
parameters.note: Schultz (1993) intact basalt lab cohesive strength; Byerlee's law high-pressure regime (>200 MPa) uses ~50 MPa (Byerlee 1978, doi:10.1007/BF00876528).

parameters.name: Cohesion (Fractured Rock Mass)
parameters.method: Hoek-Brown failure criterion/DOE (1988) jointed rock mass scaling
parameters.note: Schultz (1993) reduced cohesion for jointed/megabrecciated crustal rock masses; critical for initiating shallow fault slip.

parameters.name: Angle of Internal Friction
parameters.note: Corresponds to coefficient of friction mu = 0.60 (phi = 31 deg) for normal stress >200 MPa, mu = 0.85 (phi = 40.4 deg) at shallow depths (Byerlee 1978, doi:10.1007/BF00876528).

parameters.name: Activation Energy (Dry Diabase / Basalt)
parameters.material: Dry Columbia Diabase (Present Day / Dry Crust)
parameters.method: High temp triaxial dislocation creep lab experiments
parameters.note: Mackwell et al. (1998) dislocation creep of dry Columbia diabase

parameters.name: Creep stress exponent n (Dry Diabase)
parameters.material: Dry Columbia Diabase (Present Day / Dry Crust)
parameters.method: High temp triaxial dislocation creep lab experiments
parameters.note: Mackwell et al. (1998)
parameters.parse_note: Hand fix: the spreadsheet units cell 'Dim., MPa^-n s^-1' covered both symbols in this row. n_dry is shown in dimensionless.

parameters.name: Creep pre-exponential factor A (Dry Diabase)
parameters.material: Dry Columbia Diabase (Present Day / Dry Crust)
parameters.method: High temp triaxial dislocation creep lab experiments
parameters.note: Mackwell et al. (1998)
parameters.parse_note: Hand fix: the spreadsheet units cell 'Dim., MPa^-n s^-1' covered both symbols in this row. A_dry is shown in MPa^-n s^-1.

parameters.name: Activation Energy (Wet Diabase / Basalt)
parameters.method: High temp dislocation creep lab experiments
parameters.note: Caristan (1982) dislocation creep of wet Maryland diabase (Azuma & Katayama 2017, doi:10.1186/s40623-016-0593-z).

parameters.name: Creep stress exponent n (Wet Diabase)
parameters.method: High temp dislocation creep lab experiments
parameters.note: Caristan (1982)
parameters.parse_note: Range taken from 'n: ±0.2' in the Uncertainty/Range cell. Hand fix: the spreadsheet units cell 'Dim., MPa^-n s^-1' covered both symbols in this row. n_wet is shown in dimensionless.

parameters.name: Creep pre-exponential factor A (Wet Diabase)
parameters.method: High temp dislocation creep lab experiments
parameters.note: Caristan (1982)
parameters.parse_note: Hand fix: the Uncertainty/Range cell constrains n only ('n: ±0.2'). No range is given for A_wet. The slider uses a factor-of-three window around the tabulated value so the prefactor can be varied. Replace it when a cited uncertainty is adopted. Hand fix: the spreadsheet units cell 'Dim., MPa^-n s^-1' covered both symbols in this row. A_wet is shown in MPa^-n s^-1.

parameters.name: Activation Energy (Andesite / Plagioclase Equivalent)
parameters.material: Wet Synthetic Anorthite / Evolved Andesitic Crust
parameters.note: Rybacki & Dresen (2000) dislocation creep of wet anorthite (Q = 235 kJ/mol, n = 3.0, A = 3.98E+02 MPa^-3 s^-1).

parameters.name: Reference Viscosity (Mantle)
parameters.note: Breuer & Spohn (2006) & Plesa et al. (2018, doi:10.1029/2018JE005854)

parameters.name: Surface Temperature (Present Day Global Mean)
parameters.note: Present day value. Plesa et al. (2018) uses ~210 K global mean (~215-225 K in equatorial target regions Valles Marineris, Cerberus Fossae, and Isidis).

parameters.name: Surface Temperature (Early Mars ~3.7-4.0 Ga)
parameters.note: Early Mars value. Azuma & Katayama (2017) and Grott et al. (2007, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2006.10.001)
parameters.parse_note: Hand fix: the sheet writes the warm/wet end as '273+' (above the freezing point of pure water) with no upper number. The slider max is closed at 300 K.

parameters.name: Basal Mantle Heat Flux (Present Day)
parameters.material: Base of Crust / Mantle Heat Flow (Present Day)
parameters.note: Present day benchmark for VPLanet Plesa et al. (2018)

parameters.name: Basal Mantle Heat Flux (Early Mars)
parameters.note: Grott et al. (2007) & Ruiz et al. (2011, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2011.03.022)

parameters.name: Crustal Radiogenic Heat Production (Present Day)
parameters.note: Hahn et al. (2011) & Parro et al. (2017, doi:10.1038/srep45602):

parameters.name: Crustal Radiogenic Heat Production (Early Mars)
parameters.note: Early Mars value. Hahn et al. (2011): ~3.5x to 4.5x higher at 3.7-4.0 Ga due to shorter half-lives of 40K and 235U.

parameters.name: Fault Dip Angle (Normal Faults)
parameters.note: Standard Andersonian extensional fault dip confirmed by MOLA topographic modeling in Valles Marineris and Cerberus Fossae (Wilkins & Schultz 2003).

parameters.name: Fault Dip Angle (Thrust Faults)
parameters.note: Schultz & Watters (2001)

parameters.name: Brittle-Ductile Transition (BDT) Depth (Present Day)
parameters.material: Martian Lithosphere (Present Day Cold Stagnant Lid)
parameters.note: Present-day value. Azuma & Katayama (2017) & Plesa et al. (2018, doi:10.1029/2018JE005854)

parameters.name: Brittle-Ductile Transition (BDT) Depth (Early Mars)
parameters.note: Early-Mars / Active value. Grott et al. (2007) & Schultz & Watters (2001, doi:10.1029/2000JE001369) show major faults root into a crustal BDT at ~25-35 km depth.

parameters.name: Crustal Thickness (Global Average Moho Depth)
parameters.note: Wieczorek et al. (2022) & Knapmeyer-Endrun et al. (2021, doi:10.1126/science.abf8966): 30-72 km global average across 2-layer and 3-layer InSight models.

parameters.name: Crustal Thickness (Valles Marineris Region)
parameters.method: Bouguer gravity/topography inversion anchored from InSight
parameters.note: Wieczorek et al. (2022): thick surrounding Tharsis plateau crust (60-70 km) locally thinned to ~25-35 km beneath deepest Valles Marineris chasma floors.

parameters.name: Crustal Thickness (Cerberus Fossae / Elysium Planitia)
parameters.note: Wieczorek et al. (2022): adjacent to InSight landing site (20 ± 5 km for 2-layer or 39 ± 8 km for 3-layer model), thickening slightly toward Elysium Rise.

parameters.name: Crustal Thickness (Isidis Planitia Basin)
parameters.note: Wieczorek et al. (2022): extreme crustal thinning and mantle plug uplift beneath the Isidis impact basin (minimum thickness 6-18 km depending on reference model).

parameters.name: Crustal Density
parameters.method: Admittance, InSight seismology/ moment of inertia
parameters.note: Wieczorek et al. (2022) constrains bulk crustal density to 2850-3100 kg/m^3

parameters.name: Core Radius (Homogeneous Core)
parameters.note: Recommended baseline for VPLanet. Stähler et al. (2021)

parameters.name: Core Radius (Basal Molten Silicate Layer Model)
parameters.material: Martian Metallic Core (With 150-km Basal Magma Layer)
parameters.method: InSight diffracted seismic phases & Phobos tides
parameters.note: Samuel et al. (2023) & Khan et al. (2023, doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06586-4): a ~150 km molten silicate layer atop the core yields a smaller metallic core (1650-1675 km).

parameters.name: Core Mass (Homogeneous)
parameters.material: Martian Metallic Core (~24 wt% of planet)
parameters.note: Derived from Stähler et al. (2021) R_c = 1830 km and rho_c = 6000 ± 300 kg/m^3 (~24% of Mars total mass 6.417e23 kg); ~1.17e23 kg under Samuel et al. (2023) BML model.

parameters.name: Mantle Mass (Mantle + Crust)
parameters.material: Martian Silicate Mantle & Crust (~76 wt% of planet)
parameters.note: Stähler et al. (2021)

parameters.name: Initial Core Temperature (at CMB, Post-Accretion)
parameters.note: Breuer & Spohn (2006) & Plesa et al. (2018, doi:10.1029/2018JE005854): initial CMB temperature (2000-2400 K); present-day cooled CMB is ~1850-2000 K.

parameters.name: Bulk Silicate Uranium Abundance (U - BSM Total)
parameters.material: Bulk Silicate Mars (Mantle + Crust Combined H)
parameters.note: Taylor (2013) gives 16 ± 2 ppb U for total silicate Mars (crust + mantle); Yoshizaki & McDonough (2020, doi:10.1016/j.gca.2020.01.011) estimate 18 ppb U.
parameters.parse_note: Hand fix: the cell mixes a ± band on the first estimate with a second cited estimate (18). The slider spans min(center−Δ, second) to max(center+Δ, second).

parameters.name: Depleted Mantle Uranium Abundance (U - Subcrustal Mantle Only)
parameters.method: Mass balance (BSM minus GRS crustal reservoir)
parameters.note: Yoshizaki & McDonough (2020) & Plesa et al. (2018): present-day subcrustal mantle U after >50% partitioning into crust.

parameters.name: Bulk Silicate Thorium Abundance (Th - BSM Total)
parameters.material: Bulk Silicate Mars (Mantle + Crust Combined H)
parameters.note: Taylor (2013) gives 56 ± 6 ppb Th for total silicate Mars; Yoshizaki & McDonough (2020, doi:10.1016/j.gca.2020.01.011) estimate 68 ppb Th.
parameters.parse_note: Hand fix: the cell mixes a ± band on the first estimate with a second cited estimate (68). The slider spans min(center−Δ, second) to max(center+Δ, second).

parameters.name: Depleted Mantle Thorium Abundance (Th - Subcrustal Mantle Only)
parameters.method: Mass balance (BSM minus GRS crustal reservoir)
parameters.note: Yoshizaki & McDonough (2020): subcrustal mantle Th concentration after crustal extraction.

parameters.name: Bulk Silicate Potassium Abundance (K - BSM Total)
parameters.material: Bulk Silicate Mars (Mantle + Crust Combined H)
parameters.method: GRS K/Th ratio (~5300)/ SNC meteorite analysis
parameters.note: Taylor (2013) gives 305 ± 30 ppm K for total silicate Mars; Yoshizaki & McDonough (2020, doi:10.1016/j.gca.2020.01.011) estimate 360 ppm K.
parameters.parse_note: Hand fix: the cell mixes a ± band on the first estimate with a second cited estimate (360). The slider spans min(center−Δ, second) to max(center+Δ, second).

parameters.name: Depleted Mantle Potassium Abundance (K - Subcrustal Mantle Only)
parameters.method: GRS K/Th ratio (~5300)/ SNC meteorite analysis
parameters.note: Yoshizaki & McDonough (2020): subcrustal mantle K concentration.
